issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. There is no file or network access and no pasted coordinates. The new code only builds random row-based starting layouts (5–7 rows, 3–7 circles per row, adding up to 26) for iterations where it % 5 is 0 or 2. These are then optimised by the existing routine, so the answer is still computed by the script.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. When cnt.sum() == n, pts has shape (26, 2) and rr0 has length 26. When no valid row split is found in 500 tries, cnt is None and the earlier c0/r0 are kept. Clipping keeps centres inside [0.03, 0.97]. The final checks on the packing are unchanged.

Side effect worth knowing: the new block draws extra numbers from rng. That shifts the random sequence for every later start, so the other starts are not the same as in the incumbent. The candidate is therefore not just the incumbent plus extra starts, and any difference cannot be credited to the row layouts alone.

Numbers: candidate -2.636 against incumbent -2.6360, one run each. The difference is 0.000, so z = 0. With only one run per side the variance cannot be estimated, so z tells us little. Rejecting is consistent with the numbers: there is no improvement. Both are at about the best known result of 2.635 (2.636 is slightly above it, which is plausible from rounding or a tiny improvement).
